posts.author: CrystalCat
posts.body:
Luna engine MV
is a plugin that basically allows you to have complete control over the menus and makes overhauling them a piece of cake, and many games like Lawmage Academy uses it to create their custom menu.
The problem is, they only made the plugin for RPG MAKER MV, and i'm assuming it's not compatible with MZ.
HUD maker ultra pro
(the paid version) has the functionality to make buttons, but as far as i know it doesn't have keyboard support, and the free version doesn't have a menu screen, so i'm assuming the paid version doesn't as well. So, is there any way to either make luna engine MV compatible with MZ (legally, idk the terms of service), or a different plugin with almost the same depth that Luna MV has? im willing to go up to $60, which is the original plugins price.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
CrystalCat said:
Luna engine MV
is a plugin that basically allows you to have complete control over the menus and makes overhauling them a piece of cake
Click to expand...
Really? I've looked at it, and it looks like it's nearly as complex as coding the menu yourself in a plugin, only you have to use their custom YAML files and scripting syntax for it.
If that's simple to you, I'd suggest you do some JavaScript tutorials until you can understand and modify the code for the various windows and scenes. Then you just make your own plugin that changes it however you like. (
and
that knowledge is applicable to other parts of RPG Maker, unlike the Luna Engine scripting)
As far as commissioning anyone to make it compatible with MZ, I don't think many people purchased it, particularly not if they're able to code.
I'd look at Aerosys' plugin that ShadowDragon mentioned, or at the variety of existing alternate menu plugins, see if something is close enough to what you want that it just works or can be minorly tweaked to work.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Ironically buying paid plugins makes them harder to get help with. Unless it's Yanfly or VisuStella few people will have any given paid plugin and you're reliant on the plugin dev to help, some of which don't support the plugin anymore even if you paid for it.
If it's a free plugin anyone can download it and look at the code to help you. People aren't going to buy a plugin to look at the code to help you.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
AquaEcho said:
Ironically buying paid plugins makes them harder to get help with.
Click to expand...
This - and I recognize you said "some of which" - is
very
dependent on exactly who you bought it from.
Hakuen Studios, Kage Desu, Casper, and Ramza are the more prolific non-Yanfly/VisuStella paid authors that I'm aware of, and they all consistently provide very prompt replies to any issues.
Even Undermax I've seen on here answering questions within a day of them being asked.
So I don't know if you have anyone specific in mind, but I think the authors who don't support their work are in a minority.
It is absolutely a true statement if you mean it makes it harder to get help
from the community
with the plugin.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
KotC is Knight of the Celestial. You can see a lot of people bought
their pathfinding plugin
and asked for help and get no response.
Sometimes the dev also has personal or life matters and are away for a while and aren't responsive for that time period.
It's just a risk you take buying plugins. I guess make sure they're active first before buying it (e.g. ask them a question) and hope they don't retire/disappear/whatever when you need help down the line.
